creator: Chris Huber Reitz
name: ISO & IEC — Guidance on the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for IEC and ISO technical committees (Version 2.0, 2026)
quote: Do not use AI to substitute for your attendance, participation, or any other decision-making activity you undertake in support of writing and developing an International Standard or other publication.
quote_label: Guidance on the use of AI for IEC and ISO technical committees, v2.0 (2026), Code of conduct for technical work – spotlight on AI, (c) Participate actively (JSA bilingual copy, © ISO 2026; read live 2026-11-22)

provenance.note: DISCONFIRMATION PROBE (reserve-where-proof-is-cheap). Probe result: partly holds. Consensus decision-making (scarce proof) is reserved to humans, which fits. But Annex A says 'No' to individual AI tools to 'Refine, correct, edit, or format the draft text of a standard' and 'Yes' for ISO/IEC-licensed tools: the cheapest-to-check work is gated by tool licensing, copyright and confidentiality, not by verification cost. The line follows who supplied the tool (relational), not whether output can be checked. D1=1: 'check the sources and underlying materials'; transparency is a named principle but no logging or provenance duty. D2=2: decision-making reserved; for individual tools 'users bear complete responsibility'. D3=0: no duty to disclose AI use in drafts (the meeting-recording notice is about recording, not AI). D4=0: the bar on AI-generated text/images in ISO/IEC content is a licensing rule, not an anti-fabrication rule. D5=2: 'Do verify results or outputs of generative AI'. D6=1: check sources. Twilight false ('living document', pilots marked Maybe*, but no precedent-collapse claim).
